memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Balak's anger burned against Balaam. He struck his hands together and said to him, "I summoned you to curse my enemies, but you have blessed them these three times. Now leave at once and go home! I said I would reward you handsomely, but the LORD has kept you from being rewarded." - Num 24:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balak's frustration finally boils over. He strikes his hands together in fury and orders Balaam to go home empty-handed. Three times he sought a curse, and three times he received a blessing instead. His grand plan has utterly collapsed, and he blames Balaam for the loss of the reward.

But notice how Balak himself names the true cause: "the LORD has kept you." Even in his anger, Balak recognises that a higher power has thwarted him. He set himself against God's people, and he found himself set against God. No fury of his could change what the Lord had determined.

This is the futility of raging against God's purposes. Balak's anger accomplished nothing except to reveal his own helplessness before the Almighty. All his silver, all his sacrifices, all his persistence came to nothing. When we fight against God, we only exhaust ourselves against an immovable rock.

There is a warning and a comfort here. The warning: do not set yourself against God, for you cannot win. The comfort: no one who opposes God's people can finally succeed against them. In Christ, we are held by a God whom no enemy can overpower (Rom 8:31). The anger of the world cannot undo the blessing of God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever exhausted yourself fighting against God's clear purpose?
2. How does Balak's helplessness reveal the futility of opposing God?
3. What comfort do you find in God's power to protect His people?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from raging against Your purposes, and help me to submit to Your will. Thank You that no anger of the world can undo the blessing You have spoken over Your people in Christ. Amen.
